case-1.objects: Both A and B are required. A takes measures P,Q, transition tables p,q, a budget B, a stopping map τ, and an observable W, and produces a common density and prefix-likelihood limit L. B takes a real parameter m, fixes scalars p=(m²)⁻¹, q=m⁻¹, tables pt=U p p, qt=U q 1, a constant stopping map, and an observable C m, and produces measures P,Q of its own.
case-1.domains: Both use the product measurable space S=ℕ→Bool with discrete Bool, histories H n=Fin n→Bool, real tables T=(n:ℕ)→H n→Bool→ℝ, and a prefix filtration F n obtained by pulling back along the first n coordinates. In A, B is real, τ:S→WithTop ℕ, W:S→ENNReal, and L:S→ℝ. In B, m,p,q are real, pt,qt belong to T, the constant stopping value is in WithTop ℕ, and C m:S→ENNReal.
case-1.quantifiers: A: for every choice of the displayed inputs meeting the hypotheses, one L must satisfy the whole conclusion. The budget is for every n, P-almost every path; L's nonnegativity and convergence are P-almost everywhere, while the transferred stopping fact is Q-almost everywhere. B: for every real m≥2 there is one pair P,Q satisfying all witness properties, including the discrepancy integral bound for every n and, separately under each measure, almost every path having every coordinate k≥2 false. In both A and B the table restrictions apply to every n,h and both bits, even at histories of zero mass.
case-1.assumptions: A: the measures have probability-measure instances. For each respective pair (M,t)=(P,p),(Q,q), R₁ requires a(M,n+1,snoc(h,b))=a(M,n,h)·t n h b for every n,h,b, where a is the real prefix-event mass. R₂ requires that at every positive-P-mass history, each bit with p n h b=0 has q n h b=0. Both tables are nonnegative and sum to 1 over Bool at every history. For each n, ∑_{k<n} E P p q k x≤B P-almost surely. τ is an F-stopping time and finite P-almost surely; W is measurable and ∫⁻W² dP<⊤. B: only m≥2 is assumed externally; the probability-measure properties, recursion, support, and other conditions are requirements on the witnesses, not separate assumptions.
case-1.conclusion: A: one strongly measurable L is P-almost everywhere nonnegative and belongs to MemLp L 2 P. Along deterministic prefix lengths n→∞, D P Q n x tends to L x P-almost everywhere. The real integrals satisfy ∫L² dP≤exp B and ∫L dP=1. Q=P.withDensity(x↦ENNReal.ofReal(L x)) and Q≪P. The finite-stopping set {x | τ x≠⊤} is measurable and τ is finite Q-almost surely. Both ∫⁻W dP and ∫⁻W dQ are individually finite, and the absolute difference of their real conversions is at most √((exp B−1)·variance_P(x↦(W x).toReal)). B: the witnesses P,Q are probability measures with R₁ P pt, R₁ Q qt, R₂ P pt qt, and both tables obey the stated normalization and nonnegativity. The constant map x↦2 is an F-stopping time. Under each of P,Q separately, almost every x has x k=false for all k≥2. For every n, ∑_{k<n} ∫ E P pt qt k x dP(x)<2, using ordinary real integrals. C m is measurable, ∫⁻(C m)² dP=1, and ∫⁻C m dQ=ENNReal.ofReal m.
case-1.senses: D is Q-prefix mass divided by P-prefix mass, with Lean real division by zero equal to zero. E is zero for zero P-prefix mass and otherwise is the sum over Bool of (q−p)²/p at the observed history, under the same division convention. A bounds pathwise cumulative discrepancy P-almost surely at each horizon, not on every path or merely in expectation. A asserts almost-sure convergence, not convergence in L² or convergence of a stopped sequence; it neither requires W to be determined by τ nor asserts P≪Q or a finite Q-second moment. Individual finiteness keeps either converted integral from using ⊤.toReal=0. In B, U u v assigns true-probability u at depth zero, v at depth one after a true first bit, and zero otherwise; false-probability is the complement. B bounds sums of P-integrals, not almost-sure pathwise sums. Its terminal charge C m is not a count and is positive only when the first two bits are true; the stopping-time and zero-tail facts are distinct. B does not assert a likelihood limit, density, or variance bound.
case-1.constants: Both prefixes start at coordinate 0 (empty prefix at n=0); range n runs from 0 to n−1; table entries sum to 1. A uses the top value ⊤ for infinite stopping and extended-integral finiteness, exponent 2 for MemLp and second moments, mean density 1, moment cap exp B, and variance coefficient exp B−1, with no separately assumed B≥0. B uses m≥2, pt=U((m²)⁻¹,(m²)⁻¹), qt=U(m⁻¹,1), stopping value and tail cutoff 2, strict expected discrepancy cap 2, charge ENNReal.ofReal(m²) on the prefix (true,true) and 0 elsewhere, P-second moment 1, and Q-first moment ENNReal.ofReal m.
